title: Data mining

lead.general: Standard pattern-finding methods, run over the monthly data of this site. Each result comes with its method, its sample size and a comparison against simple guesses.
lead.expert: Patterns found by running standard mining methods over the monthly series of this site, each with its method, its sample size and a comparison against simple guesses.

leadWarning: These results are exploratory. Nothing on this page shows cause and effect.

control.bothTimings: same month and one month apart

rules.asks: Which combinations of high, normal or low months of different variables turn up together more often than chance would give?
rules.method: FP-growth on detrended monthly anomalies of the Taiwan core series, each labelled low, normal or high. One location in one month is one case. A rule is kept only when q is below {{alpha}}. Neighbouring months and places are not independent, so the q values are optimistic.

network.asks: Which pairs of variables tend to be above or below normal in the same month, or one month apart?
network.method: {{note}} Each line is a correlation that stays below q = {{alpha}} after correcting for month-to-month persistence and for the number of pairs tested. Two products of the same quantity (for example two air temperature products) are not compared with each other.
network.tableTitle: The same lines as a table

similar.asks: For one variable at one place, which other variables, here or elsewhere, went above and below normal in the same months?
similar.method: Similarity is the correlation of the monthly anomalies of two series over {{months}} months ({{first}} to {{last}}), from +1 (always together) to −1 (always opposite). {{note}} Among {{series}} series there are {{pairs}} possible pairs, so some similarity turns up by chance; {{significant}} pairs are below the limit, {{detrended}} after the trends are removed.

gap.asks: In which months, at which stations and for which model product is the monthly difference between a model temperature anomaly and the station anomaly larger?
gap.method: {{pairs}} pairs of a Taiwan weather station with GLDAS or MERRA-2 at the same place ({{stations}} stations, {{months}} pair-months). A table of group means comes first. A decision tree then tries to predict whether the difference of a month is small, medium or large, and is compared with three simple guesses. {{note}}
gap.compareLink: See the pairs and their time series on the Model vs observation page.
gap.meansTitle: Mean size of the difference by group
gap.treeTitle: Decision tree: small, medium or large difference

variants.with_target_lag: reference: also uses the previous month's class

detail.barNote: The bar is the mean of |model anomaly − station anomaly| over the months of the group; the line is a 95% interval from a bootstrap resampling whole calendar years. GLDAS segments start at the documented air-temperature steps ({{months}}). MERRA-2 is split at the same months for comparison. GLDAS has no land cell at Lanyu, so that station has a MERRA-2 pair only.
detail.newStationTitle: New station (train on the other stations, test on the one held out)
detail.accuracyNote: Accuracy is the share of test rows put in the right class. The three baselines use the most common training class, the pair's previous-month class, or the most common training class of the same calendar month. The new-station check tests a new place, not the future.
detail.lastTree: Tree of the last forward fold (trained on {{first}} to {{last}})
detail.treeNote: States are −1 (low), 0 (normal), 1 (high). A test such as “station is Taipei <= 0.5” is true for every other station. Leaf counts are training rows.
detail.confusionTitle: Last forward fold, test rows: actual class (rows) against predicted class
detail.runsNote: All {{count}} runs made are listed here; no other settings were tried.

greenness.asks: Can the other variables of a month tell whether vegetation greenness (NDVI) is low, normal or high in a Taiwan region? In this run the tree did not beat the baselines.

extra.forward_in_time_train_on_earlier_months_: Forward in time (train on earlier months, test on later months)
extra.which_features_the_trees_use_fold_by_fol: Which features the trees use, fold by fold (forward in time)
extra.which_features_the_trees_use_new_station: Which features the trees use (new station)
extra.no_pair_is_below_the_limit_with_this_set: No pair is below the limit with this setting.

detail.excludedNote: Near-duplicate variables are left out by a fixed rule in catalog order when their detrended anomalies correlate above {{limit}} (absolute value) with a variable already kept.
detail.treeMethod: Target: low, normal or high state of {{target}} in the {{table}} table. Features: this month's detrended anomalies of other variables and last month's value of each variable {{targetLag}}.
detail.sameQuantityExcluded: Variables measuring the same quantity as the target are excluded: {{names}}.
detail.validation: Validation moves forward in time: each fold tests a later block of months and trains on all earlier months. Monthly means, trend and target quantiles use training months only.
detail.baselines: Three baselines per fold use no other variable: the most common training class, the most common test class (known only afterward), and persistence from last month. Mean test accuracy over {{folds}} folds: tree {{tree}}, training majority {{training}}, test majority {{test}}, persistence {{persistence}}.
detail.foldConfusion: Fold {{fold}} test months: actual state (rows) against predicted state
detail.gapFillingNote: The tables and tree above are the {{run}} run. Trend statistics are never gap-filled.
detail.gapFillingResults: Baselines are those of the filled run. Folds above all three baselines: {{filledAbove}} of {{filledTotal}} filled, {{unfilledAbove}} of {{unfilledTotal}} unfilled. Rows usable for the tree: {{filledRows}} filled, {{unfilledRows}} unfilled.
detail.segmentedSeries: Series cut in the segmented run: {{series}}.
detail.segmentationResults: Decision tree test accuracy by fold: unsegmented {{unsegmented}}; segmented {{segmented}}. Folds above all three baselines: {{unsegmentedAbove}} of {{unsegmentedTotal}} unsegmented, {{segmentedAbove}} of {{segmentedTotal}} segmented.
